resale_co.notes: Changed from not_found to required. The Borough code has a Chapter 86, 'Zoning Use Compliance Certificate' (ecode360, blocked to direct reading). Web search results of that chapter say no one may sell or transfer title to a structure, part of a structure, lot or unit without first getting a certificate of zoning use compliance from the Zoning Officer confirming the use is permitted or a lawful pre-existing nonconforming use, that a buyer may not take title or occupy without it, and that it also helps the Tax Assessor keep records; Chapter 39 says the Zoning Officer enforces the Chapter 86 application. The exact ordinance wording could not be read, so it is not quoted; confidence is medium until the text or the Zoning Office confirms. The Borough's own application asks for the prospective buyer and settlement date, and its fee rises as settlement gets closer, which fits a sale certificate. A separate Mercantile version of the form is for rental and business licenses; the rental license page says 'A Certificate of Zoning Use Compliance is required for all new applicants, change in applicant or change of use' (rental rule). The form gives phone (609) 729-8089 (the Land Use / Construction office line); the Planning/Zoning page lists (609) 729-8090 for Rick Allen. The Construction Office (Richard Allen, Construction Official, 609-729-8089) issues Certificates of Occupancy only for building projects. Last pass put the fire bureau fees in this section by mistake; they are now only under fire_cert.

requirements: On-site inspection by the Borough Fire Prevention & Inspection Bureau; do not apply until everything is in place
Smoke alarms in each sleeping room/area, outside (within 10 feet of) each sleeping room/area, and on every level including attics
Hardwired smoke alarms must be replaced if older than 10 years after the date of manufacture; battery smoke alarms must be the 10-year sealed battery type
CO alarms outside (within 10 feet of) each sleeping room/area and on every level when there are fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage
Fire extinguisher, minimum 2A:10BC, new (current year) or tagged by a licensed fire protection agent, for each cooking area, hung in a visible location or labeled cabinet (form still lists it)
Failure to apply and have the inspection before closing carries a $1000.00 penalty to the owner

fire_cert.notes: NJ DCA lists Wildwood Crest's fire code enforcing agency as its fire department (F). The Fire Prevention page links the 2026 application. The form (April 2026) still lists a portable fire extinguisher even though P.L.2025, c.19 dropped it from state law; confirm with the Bureau. The Borough's fee ordinance (Ordinance No. 1289, posted as 'Fire Prevention Fee Ordinance May 2020', section 35-18 E) sets the sale fees at $50.00 (ten or more business days), $90.00 (four to ten), $161.00 (fewer than four) and $50.00 re-inspection; the 2026 form prints $160.00 for the shortest tier, so confirm which applies. The Bureau office number on the form is 609-729-5152; the Fire Prevention page lists 609-729-8083 for Michael Neill. It is not clear whether the $50.00 Fire Code Status Report is needed for a 1-2 family sale.
